# The test tone's Marker framing (docs/m2/04-windows-engine.md §10.3, §18.1): under IM_TEST_HOOKS with IM_ENC_FAKE the
# Opus stage re-frames each tone packet as a code 3 packet (RFC 6716 §3.2.5) whose padding is M1's 18-byte audio
# Marker (internal/media/fake/marker.go: "ISHN", rid 0, flags with 4 = beep, frame and capture ns, big endian).
#
# Each line: packet <frame> <capture_ns> <beep> <input> <framed>: the Marker's fields, an Opus packet (codes 0 to 3)
# and what the framing makes of it, in hex. opus_stage_test.cpp (MarkerGoldenBytes) writes <framed> from <input> with
# the C++ framing, which is byte for byte M1's appendOpusPadded (CBR when the frames are the same size, else VBR; old
# padding dropped); marker_golden_test.go reads every <framed> with M1's fake.ParseAudioMarker. The lines for frames 0,
# 1, 50, 51 and 100 put the Markers of the tone's packets with those numbers (capture ns = frame * 20 ms, beeps on 0,
# 50 and 100) on synthetic Opus payloads, not on the tone's encoded packets, since libopus's float output is not
# bit-exact across CPUs. The payloads cover codes 0 to 3, long frames, code 3 input with old padding (VBR and CBR), and
# one line the largest field values.
packet 0 0 1 fcfffe ff4112fffe4953484e0004000000000000000000000000
packet 1 20000000 0 fc0b30557a9fc4e90e33587da2c7ec11365b80a5caef14395e83a8cdf2173c6186abd0f51a3f6489ae ff41120b30557a9fc4e90e33587da2c7ec11365b80a5caef14395e83a8cdf2173c6186abd0f51a3f6489ae4953484e0000000000010000000001312d00
packet 50 1000000000 1
